title: Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Finally Breaks Mariah Carey’s All-Time Record for Weeks at No. 1, Eclipsing ‘All I Want for Christmas Is You’
description: There’s no long tail like a “Choosin’ Texas” long tail. Ella Langley‘s smash has just set the all-time record for the most weeks spent by a single a
body:
There’s no long tail like a “Choosin’ Texas” long tail. Ella Langley‘s smash has just set the all-time record for the most weeks spent by a single at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart: 23.  That pushes it out of the tie it held last week with Mariah Carey‘s “All I Want for Christmas,” which had been the previous record-holder with 22 weeks.

	Of course, “all time” may not last for long, since Carey’s 1994 recording seems destined to return to the No. 1 spot in December, as it always does, so regaining the all-time top position could well be in sight for Carey by January. Then again, no one has any realistic idea how much gas “Choosin’ Texas” still has in the tank, with nothing immediately poised to overtake it on the chart. Langley could Carey-proof her record-holding position by adding another few weeks to her tally before the Christmas season hits.
	

	While conventional wisdom would say that even the most ardent fans of Langley and “Choosin’ Texas” might be starting to tire of the song after such a long time — it has been charting for 48 weeks altogether now, with just under half of those weeks in the No. 1 position — the remarkable thing is that it continues to pick up new listeners. In this fragmented musical era, many people who aren’t country fans are still hearing it for the first time, as more pop stations have put their guard against Nashville down to program a smash.


	Langley’s “Dandelion” album also continues to be a big hit, if not one that will break records like the single. “Dandelion” returned to No. 1 on the Billboard 200 album chart last week, although this week it gets knocked down to No. 2 by virtue of Jhene Aiko’s “Westside Whimsy” album debuting in the top spot.
	

	Langley has a big fall ahead of her, awards news-wise as well as chart-wise. On Nov. 16, the Grammy nominations will be announced, in which Langley is expected to have a big look, perhaps finally making up for many years in which country has gone unrepresented in the top four categories. Two days after that come the CMA Awards, where she is the leading nominee. Langley recently picked up nine nominations for the CMAs, which will be broadcast out of Nashville Nov. 18.

schema.headline: Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Finally Breaks Mariah Carey’s All-Time Record for Weeks at No. 1, Eclipsing ‘All I Want for Christmas Is You’

title: Lionel Richie Undergoes Heart Procedure, ‘Will Be Back on Stage Soon’ After Canceling Next Three Shows
description: Lionel Richie will miss at least a few concert dates after being hospitalized this week and undergoing a procedure to treat atrial fibrillation, the
body:
Lionel Richie will miss at least a few concert dates after being hospitalized this week and undergoing a procedure to treat atrial fibrillation, the singer’s rep says.

	“Lionel underwent a common procedure for Atrial fibrillation (AFib),” Richie’s representative said in a statement given to Variety. “The doctor said everything went perfectly… Lionel is doing great but will take some time off and will be back on stage soon.”
	

	The procedure was said to have been undertaken on a non-emergency basis.


	The next three dates on the tour Richie has been on with Earth, Wind & Fire have been canceled. Those dates were scheduled for Saturday night in San Francisco, Sept. 30 in Chicago and Oct. 2 in Columbus, Ohio. The next shows on Richie’s concert calendar, a three-night stand at Las Vegas’ Encore Theater beginning Oct. 14, are still on, as of this writing.

	The Mayo Clinic describes the common AFib procedure as “treatment for an irregular and often very fast heartbeat… The treatment uses heat energy, cold energy or high-energy electric pulses to create tiny scars in an area of the heart. The signals that tell the heart to beat can’t pass through scar tissue. So the treatment helps block faulty signals that cause AFib.”

	Richie’s health has been in the news lately with some other canceled dates and hospitalizations, although he has seemingly quickly bounced back in each instance.

	On June 24, on the first night of the joint tour with EWF, the singer brought a show in Minneapolis to an early halt after mentioning feeling dizzy, and he subsequently canceled two dates, but he was back on stage for the tour’s June 30 stop, and told the crowd not to worry.
	

	On July 4, Richie proudly posted about the reception he had received at shows in Pittsburgh and Deroit since returning to the tour and wrote, “Thank you for every message, every kind word, and for all your love. ❤️ I’m doing well, and I’m grateful for all of you.”

	On Aug. 29, he checked himself into a hospital “out of caution,” People reported, after a performance in St. Louis, and underwent cardiac tests. The publication subsequently reported on Sept. 2 that he was checked out and had returned to Los Angeles.

title: A Geico Holiday Special? Insurance Giant’s New CMO Widens Spotlight on Entertainment
description:
Geico’s famous animated Gecko used to turn up only in TV commercials. He recently enjoyed guest-star billing on a podcast.

	The cartoonish figure w
body:
Geico’s famous animated Gecko used to turn up only in TV commercials. He recently enjoyed guest-star billing on a podcast.

	The cartoonish figure with the sophisticated accent appeared in June on WNBA player Azzi Fudd’s ‘Fudd Around and Find Out,” thanks to A.I. that allowed the character to interact with the sports star. “There’s not a lot of extra time for tinkling the ivories or playing pickleball, or whatever,” the Gecko replied when asked about hobbies.
	

	“It’s a nerve-wracking process,” confides Arianna Orpello, who joined Geico as its chief marketing officer in January. “This is one of the biggest assets that Geico has as a company. So you have to make sure it’s going to work and it’s going to work well. That takes a lot of energy to get the tools working the right way, to train the models in the right way.”


	Despite the extra attention required, more of Geico’s famous characters, ad scenarios and slogans are likely to debut in surprising venues, the executive says during a recent interview. Over three decades, Geico has “created these character worlds. You’re going to see us use them a lot more. You’re going to see them show up in places they haven’t shown up in before.”

	As a result, Geico is seeking intriguing alliances with media outlets. “Any marketer would kill to have some of these entertainment-based assets that Geico has built,” she says, adding that the company is giving new thought to how it positions itself. “What does it mean to be a modern entertainer?” Orpello asks. “Because that’s what I actually believe we are.”
	

	Geico will continue to dive into podcasts, working with iHeartMedia to launch a TikTok Podcast Network that will give it a strong hand in sponsoring creator voices and shows. Geico will back “Raiders of The Lost Podcast,” a program focused on popular movies, as well as an original effort from Diana Flores, a star quarterback with Mexico’s flag-football team. Geico has also struck up a partnership with Apartment Therapy, a media company focused on lifestyle and design, that will result in a new series centered around creative choices and investments that turn rentals into homes. The program will be distributed across Meta, TikTok and YouTube. A new alliance between Geico and Oprah Winfrey’s weekly podcast was unveiled in July.

	There is more on the way, and some of it could raise eyebrows. Look for a marketing alliance between Geico and Dairy Queen — both are part of the Berkshire Hathaway portfolio — as well as a Geico holiday special in weeks to come. The company is working on “bringing back lots of our characters into a holiday-themed world, you know, akin to — picture Frosty or Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer,” she says. “I think I can actually ask permission to do really interesting things like this.” She declined to offer more details about the special, including on what media platforms it might appear.

	Not every marketer could pull off such stuff. Media companies are paying increased attention to upstart digital advertisers that range from the online retailer Wayfair to the A.I. company OpenAI. But these relatively nascent businesses don’t often have the intellectual property to attempt some of the more intriguing — and intricate — concepts that Geico does.

	The insurance company was one of the first in the category to devise spokes-characters and clever quick-hit commercial memes in a bid to make what was once a relatively boring category stand apart. Now the field is flooded with characters from Progressive’s Flo to Liberty Mutual’s bizarre new Liberty Biberty. State Farm’s Jake character recently enjoyed a cameo role in the Netflix series “Running Point.” Geico recently allowed NBC Sports to revive the “Hump Day” talking camel that appeared in its commercials in 2013 in a promo touting the debut of NFL football on a Wednesday night. Geico wasn’t even mentioned, the executive says, and viewers still recognized the character.
	

	Building a library of ads that can evoke nostalgia or emphasize durability takes decades. Coca-Cola last year unveiled a six-minute commercial vignette from producer and creator Kenya Barris that showed the company as a “sponsor of generations” and illustrated its presence at a family-run business over many years — complete with era-appropriate logos and markings.

	Geico’s marketing history and library “is hard to match,” says Orpello. “When you look at the amount of money that has been put into building the brand of Geico and the character worlds and the value proposition, it’s really hard for a start-up to come in and try to unseat some of that.”

	As the insurance category grows ever more competitive, Geico may need its popular hits. Almost 60% of consumers with insurance policies will shop for a new one each year, says the executive. With that in mind, insurance companies need to talk to consumers every day. “You have to be relevant, top of mind, preferred, interesting, connected and there has to be recency,” she says.

	Even the smallest amounts of advertising contact are being scrutinized. When streaming users halt a selection on Hulu, Netflix or Peacock, Geico even wants more specificity in the “pause ads” that surface on screen. “If you were just watching ‘Bridgerton,’” Orpello says, a viewer ought to see “something that feels like you’re in Victorian times and the Gecko set in that environment.” In the middle of an action series, viewers who pause should seek something like the Gecko climbing a wall. How about sports? Maybe “the Gecko is actually interacting live in real time based off what’s happening in that game.”

	“We’re just trying to think about how an entertainment brand behaves, and how do we pull that through the entirety of the ad experience and the entirety of our customer experience?” says Orpello.

	The marketing executive may be feeling new heat as well. Her past jobs have largely been in the banking sector, where customers aren’t as prone to switch financial institutions. Orpello was most recently chief brand officer for Goldman Sachs, one of the nation’s most august Wall Street firms.

	Geico is putting new money behind marketing. Total underwriting expenses rose 34% in 2025 to roughly $5.5 billion and rose another 28% in the first half of this year, according to filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission from Berkshire Hathaway. Those increases were driven primarily by advertising and other customer acquisition costs, according to the company. Geico’s premiums grew more than 5% in 2025, to $45.2 billion, as the company put new effort into keeping policy holders from moving elsewhere and bringing former customers back under its umbrella.
	

	The company has dipped its toes in similar waters. In 2024, Geico unveiled a 15-minute documentary on the Gecko’s fictional origins and childhood. TV fans may recall that Geico’s popular Cavemen commercial characters were the center of an ABC sitcom in 2007, developed in part by some of the people who worked on the original ads for Geico at its longtime advertising partner, The Martin Agency. The show did not generate much positive reaction and was quickly canceled,

	Orpello acknowledges that some of her efforts may not bear fruit, but such work can’t be ignored. Without it, she says, Geico will see its standing with consumers erode.

	“I think there’s going to be a lot to play with. Some of it’s going to work. Some of it’s probably going to bomb,” she says. “We’re going to learn along the way, and I think we’re going to get better and we’re going to figure out how we continue to connect with audiences in unique ways.”

schema.headline: A Geico Holiday Special? Insurance Giant’s New CMO Widens Spotlight on Entertainment

title: How NBCUniversal Television Thrives on Collaborative Energy Between Studios and Platforms: ‘We Cheer Each Other On’
description:
From Donna Langley to Pearlena Igbokwe to Frances Berwick to Liz Jenkins, female executives largely run the show at NBCUniversal.

	In television, I
body:
From Donna Langley to Pearlena Igbokwe to Frances Berwick to Liz Jenkins, female executives largely run the show at NBCUniversal.

	In television, Igbokwe’s core team is tasked with overseeing NBCU’s television studio imprints — Universal Television, Universal Global Television and Universal Television Alternative Studio — and the scripted activity of NBC and Peacock. And that squad is dominated by women.


	Erin Underhill leads Universal Television. Beatrice Springborn heads Universal Global Television. Liza Katz is president of scripted content for NBCUniversal Entertainment. Toby Gorman is the lone male leading a Universal TV production imprint in his role as head of Universal Television Alternative Studio.
	

	Across the Universal-verse, the environment is unusually collegial and collaborative in Springborn’s experience because they’re all striving for the same thing: to make great television.

	“When you create a creative environment, it helps everyone feel like they’re part of everything you’re trying to do. That makes a huge difference, and it is a distinguishing factor for Universal,” Springborn says. “Having people who are smarter than you in a lot of different areas and having people around you who want to succeed — that makes a huge difference.”

	The strong work culture instilled by Igbokwe in her role as chairman of Universal Television Studios, NBC Entertainment and Scripted helps her teams channel their energy in the right direction, executives say.

	“We support each other. We cheer each other on,” says Underhill, whose division is home to a broad range of shows, from brawny Dick Wolf procedurals to HBO Max’s Emmy juggernaut “Hacks” to Reba McEntire’s NBC sitcom “Happy’s Place.”
	

	“When you have colleagues who have your back and are transparent and genuine, it just makes the environment a healthy one in which to thrive,” Underhill says.

	RELATED STORY: Her Rise to the Top: NBCUniversal TV Studio Chief Pearlena Igbokwe Balances Creative and Business Instincts

	Springborn underlines the point: “There’s not a sense of competition here. I have been at companies where you’re competing with people you work with. Pearlena doesn’t impose that, nor would I think she would tolerate it. I think we all subscribe to that.”

	Katz has been with NBC since 2016. The vibes are good these days in Universal City, especially after the historic studio lot received a substantial overhaul and upgrade that was completed in 2024.

	“In the current regime with Donna and Pearlena, it feels like we’re all aligned,” Katz says. “Everybody is working toward a common goal. We all just want to do great work.”



	

					Team NBCUniversal TV at the Emmy Awards: Pearlena Igbokwe, Katie Hockmeyer, Lisa Katz, Jen Neal, Frances Berwick, Liz Jenkins, Beatrice Springborn, Rachel Smith, Erin Underhill, Sharon Vuong and Toby Gorman on Sept. 14 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles.
									Chad Salvador
	



	A collaborative environment makes for a forward-thinking culture. Springborn, who joined Universal in 2020 from Hulu, notes that NBCUniversal was early to recognize the power of global television. Her division focuses on high-end series including Peacock’s Emmy-nominated “All Her Fault” and “The Five Star Weekend,” “The Day of the Jackal” and the upcoming “Dungeon Crawler Carl.”

	Two decades ago, NBCU began investing in the U.K. market through the banners Working Title and Carnival Films and Television, and by beefing up its international TV assets and capabilities in general.

	In 2011, NBCU and Carnival struck franchise gold with Julian Fellowes’ “Downton Abbey,” which emerged as a costume drama hit on ITV and PBS. Since then, the Crawley gang has yielded six seasons and three feature films (in 2019, 2022 and 2025) and promises to be an IP engine for years to come. The roots of that investment are serving NBCU well at a time when TV viewing is more global than ever before, thanks to the biggest streaming platforms.

	“We’re hearing more and more domestic studios are starting to get into the international business. A couple of them have reached out to me and been like, ‘How do you guys do this?’ Suddenly it’s become the hot thing to do,” Springborn says. “‘Downton Abbey’ was the thing that helped the international studio have such an impact and to show that you could be financially successful. We’re very proud of that franchise.”
	

	Katz emphasizes there’s a commitment to communication among the departments so that decision-making is clear. Universal Television remains an active seller of shows to networks outside NBCU’s ecosystem, in addition to supplying NBC, Peacock and Bravo. Even the mighty NBC doesn’t get everything it wants in the hunt for hot new properties, Katz observes.

	“We’re always thinking about how what we do impacts our [sibling units] because their wins are our wins and vice versa,” she says. “So, the best show wins, the best idea wins, the best project wins. Sometimes I know [Universal TV] shows are going to go outside, and that’s a bummer. But it’s always handled aboveboard and transparently.”

	Underhill notes that on days when more things go wrong than right, it helps to be able to turn to “friendly faces who get it, and who you know get you.” “It buoys you,” Underhill says of her colleagues.

	(Pictured top: Lisa Katz, Beatrice Springborn and Erin Underhill)

schema.headline: How NBCUniversal Television Thrives on Collaborative Energy Between Studios and Platforms: ‘We Cheer Each Other On’

title: Her Road to the Top: How NBCUniversal TV Studio Chief Pearlena Igbokwe Learned to Balance Business and Creative Instincts
description: By the time Pearlena Igbokwe was offered the job of president of Universal Television in 2016, she already had an impressive résumé. She’d climbed t
body:
By the time Pearlena Igbokwe was offered the job of president of Universal Television in 2016, she already had an impressive résumé. She’d climbed the ranks over 20 years at Showtime, and then excelled during a four-year stretch as head of NBC’s drama department. But the prospect of moving out of the network hierarchy to lead one of the industry’s biggest television studios was daunting. It meant shifting from buying TV shows for NBC to selling shows to networks and streamers.
	

	Igbokwe didn’t feel ready for the demands of running a large division with dozens of shows in production at any given time. But NBC Entertainment’s leaders, Bob Greenblatt and Jennifer Salke, assured her she was.




	

									Ramona Rosales for Variety
	



	“We were doing so well [at NBC], and then all of a sudden they’re like, ‘You’re going to the studio.’ And I said, ‘I’m just getting the hang of this network thing — you want to put me into something that I have to learn a different side of the business?’ And they literally said to me, ‘We know you can do it.’ Which just gave me such a boost, because I was questioning myself. But they didn’t.”

	Igbokwe would, of course, rise to the challenge. Today, she serves as NBCUniversal’s chairman of Television Studios, NBC Entertainment and Peacock Scripted originals. She oversees a wide swath of scripted programming across NBC and Peacock, and she’s NBCU’s top executive overseeing TV production through three distinct labels: Universal Television, Universal Global Television and Universal Television Alternative Studio. Igbokwe’s stature within NBCU has grown following the company’s separation in January from the linear cable channels that created Versant Media. And it’s likely to rise more as NBCU prepares to become  a standalone company after its planned spinoff from parent company Comcast in mid-2027.
	

	Donna Langley, a 2014 Power of Women honoree, hails the Nigerian-born, New Jersey-raised executive as “an important force at NBCUniversal” and in the wider industry. “Pearlena has always demonstrated a rare ability to combine commercial judgment and exceptional creative instincts with the foresight to see around corners,” Langley says. “She’s exceptional at bringing out the best in people — building strong teams, creating clarity around a shared vision and empowering those around her to do their best work. That combination of judgment, vision and leadership is rare.”

	Igbokwe’s initial caution about taking on the top TV studio job was not without merit. Her elevation to president of Universal Television proved to be a challenge. From a few early missteps, she discovered the importance of investing her time in being an effective manager of people. “What I’ve learned is that being the boss is different from being a leader. The boss is the person who just tells you what to do. Being a leader is the person who has to inspire other people to do their best work,” Igbokwe says.

	Greenblatt, who worked with Igbokwe at Showtime from 2003-2010, was the one who recruited her to NBC in 2012. He saw that Igbokwe wasn’t just a good executive; she established trust with the showrunners and producers on signature Showtime series such as “Dexter,” “Nurse Jackie” and “Soul Food.” “Over the years I have seen her grow to the point where she mastered the skills of talent relations,” Greenblatt says.

	Igbokwe has maintained her relationship-centric approach to her work, even as her roster as a studio chief has expanded to include such notables as Dick Wolf, Lorne Michaels, Tina Fey and Robert Carlock, Michael Schur, Greg Daniels and Amy Poehler.

	“All the people at that studio see her as a partner. She has helped grow their businesses,” Greenblatt says.

	RELATED STORY: How NBCUniversal Thrives on Collaborative Energy Between Studios and Platforms

	In hindsight, Igbokwe feels fortunate to have had her formative experience as a programming executive at Showtime, where she had the luxury of focusing on only a handful of shows. She was able to devote the time she needed to become familiar with every part of each program. “I felt the same level of responsibility for the shows as the producers did,” Igbokwe says, “and I just felt like we all had this shared collective success. I was in the ‘Dexter’ writers’ room with them, and they saw me as careful a steward of the show as they were.”
	

	And some things don’t change. Igbokwe is now one of NBCUniversal’s most senior leaders, but she still gets into the nitty-gritty on projects where she knows she can make a difference. Will Packer, a prolific producer of movies and TV shows, says she was “indispensable” to the production of “Fight Night: The Million Dollar Heist,” his 2024 limited series for Peacock starring Kevin Hart. “She never hesitates to get in the trenches with her creative partners, a skill she’s honed over a career few can rival, and one that’s woefully lacking in many executives,” Packer says. He also praises Igbokwe as a leader, citing her “ability to push those around her to deliver at the highest level they’re capable of while still feeling like a true partner and collaborator.”


	In 1971, when Igbokwe was 6, her family fled their homeland as refugees amid the civil war that ensued in the chaotic years after Nigeria gained independence from Great Britain. The life-changing migration to the United States ended with the family settling in Montclair, New Jersey, where television became young Igbokwe’s best friend. It helped her navigate her new world.

	The oldest of three children, Igbokwe was a good student. With assistance from the nonprofit A Better Chance, she attended an all-girls prep school in New Jersey that put her on the path to undergrad at Yale University and then an MBA from Columbia University.

	During her time in New Haven, she spent two summers working in the NBC Summer Associates program, where she was exposed to the inner workings of the network as a research associate. The experience opened her eyes to the potential for a career in entertainment.

	“I think so much about my life’s journey and especially my professional journey. It’s certainly not an impossible journey, but it’s improbable. The older I get, the less I think that things are improbable, because I come from such an improbable place — a child in the middle of a civil war in Nigeria,” she says. “And then my family was one of the few that got to come here.”

	The weight of that opportunity has stayed with her. “So many people died in that civil war in Nigeria. So many people could not leave,” she says. “Sometimes when I look back at it all, I say, ‘What are the chances? What are the odds?’”

	Coming back to NBC more than 25 years after her days running around 30 Rock in Summer Associates program was extremely gratifying for Igbokwe, who is a natural overachiever. 
	

	“The thing I always remember is that whatever I do, it’s in service to a company that needs to also do something else — make money. I wasn’t making TV shows as home movies; it’s in the context of a business,” she says. “I love the mix of the strategic and the financial and the creative aspects of this job. I love it because they feed off of each other. If you do something great creatively that’s really successful, it helps the balance sheet. But you have to manage the balance sheet in a way that allows you to do more of those things and to make those decisions. You don’t get to be a senior leader without always understanding the business implications of what you’re doing.”

	Igbokwe is statuesque and vivacious. She has a distinctive laugh that echoes and a brightness to her smile that commands attention. She can be fierce and warm all at once. In 2012,as Igbokwe settled into a more high-profile perch as the leader of drama development for NBC, it was an adjustment for some people in NBC’s orbit.

	“One guy in particular took me to lunch and said, ‘How’d you get this job?’ He had no qualms asking me that,” Igbokwe says, shaking her head.

	As an immigrant, Igbokwe got his message loud and clear. “There’s always that sense that you’re a bit of an outsider,” she says. “I’ve always been underestimated by a lot of people. But not by the right people who mattered, the people who entrusted me with opportunities. You can have 10 people doubting you — ‘Is she the right person for that job? — but all you need is one or two to say, ‘You’re the right person for that job.’ That has really been the trajectory of my career.”  




	

									Courtesy of the American Civil Liberties Union
	


	
		Charity Spotlight: A Better Chance	

	Pearlena Igbokwe’s connection to A Better Chance could not be more personal. The New York-based nonprofit helps high-potential students of color secure admission to top public and private high schools, so they can go to college and become leaders across the public and private sectors. A Better Chance was founded in 1963 by a group of New England educators in the heady moment when New Frontier idealism met Civil Rights Movement activism. Nearly 15 years later, Igbokwe became one of the hundreds of students helped each year by ABC. Then a teenager growing up in Montclair, New Jersey, Igbokwe received support from ABC to attend Kent Place, a renowned all-girls school with a rigorous college-prep program. 

	It was life-changing, Igbokwe says. “It opened a door to a world that I didn’t know existed,” she recalls. “In the beginning, I felt somewhat out of place. But a large part of what the program did was teach us that we belonged there.”

	Indeed. Igbokwe’s impressive rise in Hollywood makes her a powerful example of what ABC hopes to achieve, student by student. Now led by president and CEO Francisco Tezén, ABC works with 200 partner schools to arrange financial aid for about 350 students every year. In 2000, Oprah Winfrey threw a spotlight on ABC by giving it a $10 million charitable donation.
	

	To date, ABC counts about 20,000 prominent people in its alumni network, including former Massachusetts Gov. Deval Patrick and cultural commentator Roxane Gay.

title: ‘Kim’s Convenience’ Star Andrew Phung Joins Quentin Lee’s Zombie Comedy ‘Curse of Undead’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Andrew Phung, an eight-time Canadian Screen Award winner known for “Kim’s Convenience” and “Run the Burbs,” is boarding Quentin Lee‘s horror-comedy
body:
Andrew Phung, an eight-time Canadian Screen Award winner known for “Kim’s Convenience” and “Run the Burbs,” is boarding Quentin Lee‘s horror-comedy “Curse of Undead” as star and producer.

	Phung will play protagonist Pancho Dang in the Canada-Philippines co-production, which follows a struggling Canadian filmmaker battling a zombie outbreak unleashed by a Filipino sorcerer, while uncovering a curse tied to the documentary meant to launch his career. The screenplay, based on an original story by Lee, was written by Lee and New York Times bestselling author Grady Hendrix, whose novels include “My Best Friend’s Exorcism,” adapted into a feature by Amazon Studios, and “How to Sell a Haunted House.”
	

	Phung and Lee met at the 2024 Canadian Screen Awards, where a comedy special co-produced by Lee and Cindy Au Yeung, “Comedy Invasion,” took home the top prize in its category. When Lee and Au Yeung reworked “Curse of Undead” into a Canada-Philippines co-production, Lee brought the project to Phung, who signed on after connecting with the screenplay.


	“This is the type of movie I’ve always wanted to make. It’s big, it’s bold, it’s a zombie horror movie like you’ve never seen before. The script and story just jump off the page. I can’t wait to help Quentin and his team bring this project to life,” said Phung.

	“When I first met Andrew at the Canadian Screen Awards, I was already a huge admirer of his comic brilliance,” said Lee. “When Cindy and I decided to reimagine ‘Curse of Undead’ as a Canada–Philippines co-production, Andrew immediately came to mind as our Pancho. I was thrilled that he loved the screenplay and wanted to join us – not only as our leading man, but also as a producer.”
	

	Roger Garcia, former executive director of the Hong Kong International Film Festival and the Asian Film Awards Academy, serves as executive producer and began developing the screenplay with Lee more than a decade ago. Lee, Au Yeung and Phung will finance and produce through British Columbia-based Margin Films Ltd., with production targeted for winter 2027.

	Lee is also preparing to launch the third season of “Comedy InvAsian,” the Asian American stand-up comedy series he created with Koji Steven Sakai, on Oct. 1 via AAM.tv, Amazon Prime Video, Hoopla and Tubi.

title: Fantastic Fest 2026 Awards Winners List: ‘Ghost in the Cell,’ ‘Girl in the Night’ and ‘Adult Supervision’ Take Top Feature Honors (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Fantastic Fest, the annual Austin-based celebration of genre filmmaking, has announced top honors for its films in competition.

	“Our winning films
body:
Fantastic Fest, the annual Austin-based celebration of genre filmmaking, has announced top honors for its films in competition.

	“Our winning films embody distinctive and powerful voices from a wide range of cultures, and the exciting new generation of talent shaping the future of genre cinema,” Annick Mahnert, director of programming, said in a statement. “It is our privilege to give these exciting filmmakers the platform and recognition they deserve, and we are so grateful for our jurors to help us celebrate the very best in genre filmmaking.” 
	

	The winning films included:

title: National Hispanic Media Coalition Announces 2026 Cohort for Series Scriptwriters Program (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
The National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC) announced its 2026 cohort of participants for its annual Series Scriptwriters Program (SSP).

	Ten Lati
body:
The National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC) announced its 2026 cohort of participants for its annual Series Scriptwriters Program (SSP).

	Ten Latine writers from across the country were selected for an eight-week intensive, where they will develop scripts for an original television pilot that will be reviewed by SSP studio partners, including The Walt Disney Company, NBCUniversal and Netflix. They will also have access to networking opportunities within the industry.
	

	Barbara Muschietti, the producer of “It,” “It: Chapter Two” and “The Flash,” provided the opening remarks for the program’s welcome ceremony on Monday. She also served as the co-creator of the HBO original series “It: Welcome to Derry.”


	The NHMC Series Scriptwriters Program has helped accelerate the careers of Latine storytellers for 24 years, supporting more than 200 writers in developing their projects. Alumni from the program have gone on to work on notable shows such as AMC’s “Interview With the Vampire,” CBS’s “Matlock,” NBC’s “Chicago Fire,” NBC’s “Lopez vs. Lopez,” Starz’s “The Serpent Queen,” Apple TV+’s “Acapulco” and NBC’s “Something Wicked,” the upcoming reboot of “Bewitched.”

	Working to eliminate hate, discrimination and racism toward Latine communities, the NHMC is a women-led non-profit civil and human rights organization. The program has also developed initiatives including Latinx Stream Showcase, Youth in Entertainment and media advocacy fellowship programs while also advocating for the Affordable Connectivity Program, Lifeline Program and Net Neutrality protections.
	

	The cohort of participants for the 2026 Series Scriptwriters Program includes the following:

	Alix Mendoza

	Angelica López

	Brandon Burkhart

	Francis Fuster

	Gisella Bustillos

	Iris Almaraz

	Johanna Rosario

	Matthew Gonzalez

	Michael Gonzalez

	Sergio Garcia Bennet

	Zan Poka

title: Jessica Lange Speaks Out on ‘American Horror Story 13’ Return, From Playing Secret Fifth Character to Begging for a Musical Number
description:
Jessica Lange is not only reprising her four previous “American Horror Story” roles in Season 13 — she’s debuting a new one. 

	When asked on “Good
body:
Jessica Lange is not only reprising her four previous “American Horror Story” roles in Season 13 — she’s debuting a new one. 

	When asked on “Good Morning America” on Tuesday what made her want to return to Ryan Murphy’s horror anthology series, Lange said, “It really was just the idea of bringing those four characters back —and one mystery character that I’m not going to [spoil].”


	Later in the interview, when Sam Champion prodded Lange to say more about the fifth character, she hinted that fans may have a chance of deducing who it is. “There is a fifth character, but I won’t say who that is, and I’d be curious if anybody can figure it out,” she said.
	

	Lange’s four known characters include Constance Langdon from Season 1, “Murder House”; Sister Jude Martin from Season 2, “Asylum”; Fiona Goode from Season 3, “Coven”; and Elsa Mars from Season 4, “Freak Show.” According to Lange, “Constance was Ryan’s favorite character from the beginning, so she is featured pretty much throughout the whole thing. The character that I really loved playing was Elsa.”


	Lange also teased a musical number she’ll perform as “one of the characters” in “American Horror Story” Season 13, without specifying who. “I have to beg, borrow and plead to get anybody to let me sing,” she joked. When Robin Roberts suggested the number could earn her a Grammy and complete her EGOT, Lange seemed to hint that the character won’t be a strong singer. “I’m going to have to find a Grammy a different way.” Champion asked, “You’re not convinced this is the one?” “No, and neither will you when you see it,” Lange said, laughing. 
	

	“American Horror Story” Season 13 premieres on FX on Thursday.

title: Jensen Ackles to Star in Crime Thriller Series ‘Rules of Prey’ at MGM+
description:
Jensen Ackles is set to star in the thriller series “Rules of Prey,” which has been greenlit at MGM+. 

	The eight-episode series is based on the bo
body:
Jensen Ackles is set to star in the thriller series “Rules of Prey,” which has been greenlit at MGM+. 

	The eight-episode series is based on the book of the same name by John Sandford (a.k.a John Camp), which is the first in Sandford’s “Prey” novel series that focus on former police detective Lucas Davenport. Production is set to begin this month in Toronto. It will premiere on MGM+ in the U.S., United Kingdom, Ireland, Germany, Spain, Italy, Belgium, Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Chile.
	

	The official logline states that the show follows Davenport (Ackles), “formerly a detective in the Minneapolis Police Department, drawn out of seclusion back into law enforcement to investigate a series of confounding murders designed to send a message specifically to him. When an ingenious serial killer begins murdering Minneapolis citizens, Davenport, a brilliant polymath and unconventional investigator, takes the case, sparking an intense psychological duel with an equally intelligent adversary. As Davenport deciphers the killer’s twisted moral code and personal vendetta, he must match wits with a predator operating by his own rules of justice, risking everything to stop a killer who sees their conflict as the ultimate game.” 


	“Jensen Ackles’ classic leading man charisma, combined with Bruce Terris’ skillful adaptation of John Sandford’s enduringly popular Prey series is an excellent fit for MGM+,” said Michael Wright, global head of MGM+. “The series delves into the psychological depth and suspense that made Sandford’s novels unmissable reading and continues MGM+’s commitment to bringing classic Hollywood storytelling to modern audiences.”
	

	The series hails from Bruce Terris (“DTF St. Louis,” “Patriot”), who also serves as showrunner and executive producer. Ackles will executive produce in addition to starring. Charles Gogolak and Matt Leipzig of Modern Literary Arts executive produce along with Howard Braunstein, Michael Jaffe, John Requa, Glenn Ficarra and John Weber. Sandford serves as co-producer. Daniel Sackheim will direct the pilot and episode two in addition to executive producing. MGM Television and Take 5 Productions produce. Terris is currently under an overall deal at MGM. 

	Ackles has a longstanding relationship with Amazon MGM Studios, beginning with his time playing Soldier Boy on the hit Prime Video series “The Boys.” He will reprise that role in the prequel “Vought Rising,” which is due out in 2027. He also previously starred in the Prime Video series “Countdown” for one season. He is best known for his 15-season run on the beloved series “Supernatural,” which ran from 2005-2020. 

	The first Lucas Davenport book was published in 1989. There have been 36 books in the series total, with Sandford most recently publishing “Revenge Prey” in 2026. 

	Terris is repped by CAA, Modern Literary Arts, and Lichter Grossman. Ackles is repped by Gersh and attorney PJ Shapiro. Sandford is repped by CAA. Sackheim is repped by Independent Artist Group, Industry Entertainment and Jared Levine.

	Deadline first reported the series order.

schema.headline: Jensen Ackles to Star in Crime Thriller Series ‘Rules of Prey’ at MGM+

title: Nick Reiner Claims $325K Inheritance From Famous Grandpa Is Exempt From Slayer Law
description:
Nick Reiner
                          My Parents' Case Doesn't Block Grandpa's Money
body:
Nick Reiner
                          My Parents' Case Doesn't Block Grandpa's Money
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 22, 2026
                            8:30 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Nick Reiner says a large chunk of the money locked up in his trust should be off-limits in the fight over whether he gets access to the funds ... because it came from his famous grandfather, late actor Carl Reiner.
      
    
            Court docs obtained by TMZ show Nick's legal team is arguing California's Slayer Statute -- that basically says no one should profit from their own crime -- does not apply to money Carl left him because Nick is not accused of causing his grandfather's death.
      
    
            According to the filing, a substantial portion of the funds currently held in Nick's trust came from Carl's estate plan, which included similar distributions to his other grandchildren.
      

            Nick's lawyers say at least $325,000 was transferred into his trust account at JPMorgan Chase in December 2024 ... a year before Nick allegedly murdered his parents.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            They claim other distributions from Carl's estate may have also been deposited into the trust, though it's not yet clear how much money came from his grandfather or why it was placed there instead of being given directly to Nick.
      
    
            Carl died in June 2020.
      
    
            Nick's legal team says money inherited from Carl did not come from or through Nick's parents, Rob and Michele Reiner, and should therefore be separated from the rest of the trust money and released to him.
      
    
            Even if the money was properly placed in the trust, Nick argues the Slayer Statute still cannot be used to withhold it because Nick has not been accused of causing his grandfather's death.
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported, Nick has been fighting for access to the family trust while awaiting trial on two counts of first-degree murder for allegedly killing his parents.

title: Nolan Wells Death: See the Tense Written Exchange Between D.A. and Family Lawyers
description:
Nolan Wells
                          Family Lawyers, Prosecutors Had Tense Exchange ...
body:
Nolan Wells
                          Family Lawyers, Prosecutors Had Tense Exchange ...
                          Read The Back-and-Forth
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 22, 2026
                            8:22 AM PDT
                                                                            
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Here's the heated exchange between lawyers for Nolan Wells' family and prosecutors in Mississippi ... and it's chock full of drama and friction.
      
    
            The correspondence between Jackson County D.A. Angel Myers McIlrath and several of the family's attorneys was recently released as part of a grand jury report ... and it appears to show major communication issues between the two sides.
      
    
    
              
                
  
    
            The D.A. sent an email to Gary Bufkin, Esq., July 29 ... stating there was no legal authority requiring her office to share information with civil counsel during an active investigation, adding that there was a process for death investigations, and she didn't think it was appropriate to deviate from it.
      

            That said, in another email, the D.A. does try to facilitate further examination of Nolan's body by forensic pathologist Dr. Roger Mitchell, the man who conducted the independent autopsy on Nolan ... and she says she even wants him to testify in front of the grand jury.
      
    
            The review of Nolan's cell phone also raised some issues ... the lawyers push for a joint examination alongside the FBI -- while the D.A. pushes back.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            As you know ... the D.A. announced that criminal charges aren't being filed in Nolan's death.
      
    
            According to the Mississippi State Medical Examiner's autopsy report, Nolan's manner of death was ruled "undetermined" -- and the Grand Jury found "that the position of, the condition of, time of discovery, and location of Mr. Wells body is consistent with drowning."
      
    
            D.A. McIlrath put out a video in which she repeated that there's "no evidence" to suggest Nolan's death was "racially motivated."
      
    
            After the Grand Jury's decision, Edward Andrew Paltzik, an attorney for Nolan's friends, told us, "We said it all along: Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo, and Morgan Seymour were always completely innocent. There was never any doubt. They are terrific people."

title: Carrot Top: Read Alleged $2 Million Demand Comedian Received Days Before Suicide Attempt
description:
Carrot Top
                          Read $2M Demand Comedian Was Sent Days Before Suicide Attempt
body:
Carrot Top
                          Read $2M Demand Comedian Was Sent Days Before Suicide Attempt
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 21, 2026
                            6:15 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 22, 2026
                                8:09 AM PDT
                                    
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Carrot Top was handed a $2 million demand just days before his attempted suicide ... and within hours, his lawyer was telling the court the comedian was being extorted ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            TMZ obtained a pair of emails laying out the heated legal battle that unfolded last Monday -- four days before Carrot Top was hospitalized.
      
    
    
              
                
  
    
            In the first message, Brian Evans -- whom Carrot Top's team has accused of extortion -- proposed a $2 million deal to end the legal fight involving himself, Carrot Top -- real name Scott Thompson -- and several others.
      

            Evans said everyone would drop their claims and keep the deal private ... and he even gave Carrot Top's team until Wednesday afternoon to accept.
      
    
            Hours later, Carrot Top's attorney emailed an assistant for Florida Judge Shari Africk Olefson, accusing Evans of waging a "campaign of extortion." The attorney claimed Evans was demanding millions or else he would file "false, malicious and incendiary materials" in the court record for the press to pick up.
      
    
            He asked the court for immediate emergency relief, accusing Evans of using "extortion and blackmail" to malign Carrot Top.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Brian adamantly denies all claims of wrongdoing. He previously told TMZ ... "I never threatened - ever - to post any video anywhere in exchange for a settlement. … The video they are discussing - as I made very clear - was deleted a long time ago in accordance with the prior settlement."
      
    
            We reached out to Brian for comment on the letter, he told TMZ, "You’re talking about a global settlement that was to resolve all cases, including cases that were raised post-settlement."
      
    
            "Do you not see what they are doing? ... They are taking Rule 408 settlement communications and trying to annihilate my character to deflect from their own behavior," Brian said.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            He continued, "This is nothing more than them attempting damage control from their conduct, as is often the case when people are accused of what they have been. Scott is not a victim. Even Weinstein's victims were being called extortionists because that’s their only defense, and Thompson to this very day has never filed an answer to the complaint."
      
    
            Brian ended, "It’s one-sided and orchestrated to just make him look like the victim while discrediting the actual ones."
      
    
            TMZ broke the story ... Carrot Top was hospitalized last Friday after an attempted suicide, which we learned was from a suspected overdose from prescription drugs.
      
    
            If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 or chat 988lifeline.org.

title: Hayden Panettiere's Cause of Death Revealed
description:
Hayden Panettiere
                          Cause of Death Revealed
body:
Hayden Panettiere
                          Cause of Death Revealed
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 22, 2026
                            7:18 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 22, 2026
                                8:54 AM PDT
                                    
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Hayden Panettiere's cause of death has been revealed ... the actress died from fentanyl and several other drugs.
      
    
            The Greenville County Coroner, in a report obtained by TMZ, ruled Hayden's manner of death as an accident. She was also found to have the following in her system -- Alprazolam (generic Xanax), a muscle relaxant called Methocarbamol, and Quetiapine ... a drug used to treat bipolar disorder, schizophrenia and major depression.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            As we reported ... Hayden died August 16 inside a Greenville, South Carolina, apartment after traveling from L.A. with her boyfriend, Brian Hickerson.
      

            She was later found unresponsive by Brian and his brother Zach. Brian gave her Narcan to try and revive her, and they performed CPR until paramedics arrived.
      
    
            Her autopsy previously found "no signs of trauma" that would have contributed to her death.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Paramedics performed advanced cardiac life support and chest compressions ... but Hayden could not be resuscitated and was pronounced dead at 2:32 PM.
      
    
            Shortly after her death, the actress' Los Angeles home was searched by federal drug agents ... with sources telling TMZ the officials were looking for evidence tied to her drug dealer.
      
    
            We reported earlier ... officials believed at the time of the search that she took an oxy pill laced with fentanyl just before her death.
      
    
            Meanwhile, her West Hollywood neighbors had long suspected a drug dealer had been dropping off drugs to her home.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Sources told us ... Hayden and her drug dealer sent a "slew of messages" about drugs, something the DEA is focused on in their investigation.
      
    
            Hayden was best known for starring in "Heroes" and "Nashville," as well as roles in "Remember the Titans" and the 'Scream' franchise.
      
    
            She was only 36.

title: Nolan Wells: No Criminal Charges To Be Filed, Medical Examiner Determines Death Was Drowning
body:
Nolan Wells' death has been determined to be "consistent with a drowning" ... months after the 18-year-old vanished during a Fourth of July boating trip to Mississippi's Horn Island.
      
    
            According to the Mississippi State Medical Examiner's autopsy report, Nolan's manner of death was ruled "undetermined."
      
    
            “The Grand Jury finds that the position of, the condition of, time of discovery, and location of Mr. Wells’ body is consistent with drowning,” the report read. The Grand Jury, which consisted of 13 men and 10 women, was impaneled on April 20, per local reports. They met again on September 14 and ended on September 18. The report also noted Nolan did not have cocaine in his system, despite rumors.
      

            The report noted that bruising was found on the back of Nolan’s head … but it was not considered a fatal injury. 
      
    
            Jackson County District Attorney Angel Myers McIlrath revealed the grand jury came back with a "no true bill" ... meaning they did not find anybody was responsible for Nolan's death.
      
    
      
      There will be no persons charged in the death of Nolan Wells. District Attorney Angel Myers McIlrath addresses the public regarding the unanimous decision returned by the Grand Jury: pic.twitter.com/KfTYL5pFmx
              @wakandagodd
  
    
            The D.A. released a video in which she said there was "absolutely no evidence" to support the claim that Nolan’s death was “racially motivated.”
      
    
            "The death of Nolan Wells has devastated our community. Outsiders and influencers have attempted to exploit Nolan’s death to divide and create chaos here, but we are better," the D.A. added.
      
    
            Edward Andrew Paltzik, an attorney for Nolan's friends, tells TMZ, "NO TRUE BILL."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            He continued, "We said it all along: Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo, and Morgan Seymour were always completely innocent. There was never any doubt. They are terrific people."
      
    
            The state conducted Nolan's autopsy July 7 -- one day after his body was found along the Horn Island shoreline -- but the findings remained under wraps for weeks.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            As we reported ... Nolan traveled to the island with friends on July 4 but never made it back to the mainland. His friends said they tried to convince him to leave around 4:30 PM, but he refused.
      
    
            Nolan was reported missing that night ... and his body was discovered two days later, near where he was last seen alive.
      
    
            Authorities initially believed Nolan drowned and said they had found no evidence of a crime ... but his family repeatedly questioned that explanation and launched its own investigation.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            The family hired attorney Ben Crump and arranged an independent autopsy, which found a large area of red discoloration at the back of Nolan's head ... a finding the examiner said could indicate an injury.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            However, the independent examiner listed both Nolan's cause and manner of death as undetermined pending further investigation.
      
    
            Crump said the examiner did not receive all of Nolan's organs -- including his throat and lungs -- or the autopsy photos needed to help determine the circumstances when he entered the water.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Crump's team also hired audio experts to review the full Sea Tow call placed after one of the group's boats began taking on water ... along with oceanic engineering experts to study the tides and the location where Nolan's body was found.
      
    
    
              
                
  
    
            The United Cajun Navy later compiled a separate report using photos, videos, coordinates and witness material. The group said Nolan's last sighting was sometime between 3:23 and 4:27 PM -- leaving a major gap in the timeline before the boat he arrived on departed at 4:31 PM.
      
    
            Nolan's family has maintained they will continue pressing for answers about what happened during his final hours.

schema.headline: Nolan Wells: No Criminal Charges To Be Filed, Medical Examiner Determines Death Was Drowning
